title: Synthesis of Keratin-based Nanofiber for Biomedical Engineering
protocol: Under a fume hood, add 20 ml of peracetic acid to 980 ml of deionized (DI) water to prepare 1,000 ml of 2% wt/vol peracetic acid solution (PAS).
Add 12.2 g of Tris Base to 1,000 ml of DI water and stir until completely dissolved to prepare 1,000 ml of 100 mM Tris base solution (TBS).
Pour 4 ml of concentrated hydrochloric acid into 30 ml of DI water in a fume hood to prepare diluted hydrochloric acid solution (DHAS).
Procure approximately 20 g of human hair clippings that have not been chemically treated or altered.
Wash the hair thoroughly, by hand, with warm water and soap, using deionized (DI) water for the final rinse.
Place the washed hair into two 600 ml beakers and put them in an 80 ºC oven for 1 hr.
Drain the liquid from the bottom of the beaker and place back in the oven until the hair is completely dry.
Divide dried hair evenly between the 600 ml beakers, placing 10 g of hair into each beaker.
Pour 500 ml of PAS into each beaker making sure to cover all of the hair.
Cover the beakers with parafilm and store for 12 hr.
Separate the hair from the PAS using a 500 µm sieve.
Collect waste PAS in a separate container.
Rinse the hair thoroughly with DI water to remove leftover PAS.
Place rinsed hair in a 500 ml flask.
Pour 400 ml of TBS into the flask, covering the hair.
Place the flask in a shaking bath set to 38 ºC and 65 rpm for 1 hr.
Remove the flask from the shaking bath after 1 hr.
Pour 400 ml of keratin extraction solution (KES) into a 1,000 ml beaker.
Pour 400 ml of DI water into the flask to cover the hair again.
Place the flask back in the shaking bath for another hour.
Remove the flask from the shaking bath after an additional hour.
Pour the remaining 400 ml of KES into the 1,000 ml beaker with previously collected KES.
Discard the hair by dumping it out and disposing of it in a trash receptacle.
Fill rotodistiller bath to the top line with distilled water and set to 90 ºC.
Set rotation speed to 200 rpm.
Turn on coolant chiller-pump and set to -10 ºC.
Monitor pH of KES using a pH meter.
Slowly add 1 mM DHAS to KES until reaching pH 7.0, stirring gently as solution is added.
Pour neutralized KES into the 500 ml round-bottom flask until quarter full.
Run distiller according to manufacturer's protocol for 1.25 hr.
Repeat step of adding DHAS and pouring KES into the flask until all KES has been distilled.
Ensure that the flask is connected tightly throughout the process.
Pour KES solution equally into 12 separate 14 ml conical tubes.
Centrifuge the tubes at 1,050 x g for 10 min.
Pour the centrifuged KES into a clean beaker, avoiding collected debris.
Repeat the process until all KES has been processed.
Fill a 2,000 ml graduated cylinder with DI water.
Cut dialysis tubing to 24 inches and clip one end shut.
Dip the tubing in DI water for flexibility.
Open the non-clipped end of the tubing and pour 60 ml of centrifuged KES into it.
Close this end of the tubing with a clip.
Place the dialysis tube in the 2,000 ml cylinder of DI water and allow to sit for 24 hours.
Change the DI water every 3 to 4 hours during the first day.
Empty the dialyzed KES solution into capped jars, leaving space at the top.
Freeze the jars containing the KES solution at -20°C for 24 hours.
Set the lyophilizer to -86 °C.
Remove the frozen KES jars from the freezer and place them in freeze dryer ampoules without caps.
Place seals on the ampoules and turn the knob to create a vacuum pressure of 0.133 mBar.
Lyophilize the samples for approximately 48 hours, until all moisture is removed.
Remove Keratin Powder from the lyophilizer and weigh it.
Add DI water to the Keratin powder to create a 10% weight/weight Keratin solution.
Obtain PCL (ε-caprolactone polymer, Mn 70 - 90 kDa) and trifluoroethanol (TFE).
Prepare a 10% by weight PCL in TFE by stirring overnight and obtain a homogeneous mixture.
Add keratin into the PCL solution dropwise to create 10 ml PCL/keratin solutions of 90:10, 80:20, 70:30, and 60:40 ratios.
Use a vortexer to obtain a homogeneous mixture of PCL/Keratin solution before electrospinning.
Place approximately 8 ml of the PCL/keratin solution in a 10 ml disposable syringe fitted with a 0.5-mm diameter plastic tube.
Place the syringe in a syringe pump where the flow rate is set to be 2.5 ml/hr.
Apply voltage to the tip of the needle connected to the tube positioned ~23 cm from the fiber collecting drum and ~30 degrees from the horizontal.
Apply a 19 - 22 kV voltage to the tube and rotate the collector drum at around 200 rpm.
Cut the sample into 60 mm by 8 mm.
Record the thickness using a digital micrometer.
Attach five samples of each composition to the tensile tester.
Use a custom-designed specimen holder to attach the sample.
Sandwich the sample between specimen holders made from an index card with double-sided tape.
Apply a 10 N load cell with a displacement rate of 10 mm/min.
Record extension and load values through software according to the software protocol.
Calculate stress by dividing the force by the area of the sample tested.
Calculate strain by dividing the change in length by the initial length.
Generate the stress-strain curve by plotting stress on the y-axis and corresponding strain value on the x-axis.
Calculate the Young's modulus from the linear region where the slope equals the modulus of elasticity.
Determine tensile strength from the stress-strain plot by taking a 0.2% offset in strain and drawing a parallel line to the linear region curve.
Perform statistical analysis of the mechanical data obtained in triplicate using one-way analysis of variance with analysis software.
Cut a 2 cm² section of the fiber and attach it to a SEM stage using copper tape.
Place the stage inside the sputter coater and coat with gold at 15 mA for 1 min and 30 sec.
Load the sample into the chamber of the SEM.
Observe the fiber samples.
Place the 2 cm² section of the electrospun nanofiber membrane in a magnetic holder.
Purge the system with dry air before testing.
Obtain spectra for 200 scans using FTIR to characterize chemical bonding between PCL and keratin.
Analyze the spectra using standard software according to the manufacturer's protocol.
Cut fibers into 16 mm² samples.
Fix each sample to coverslips with a 12 mm diameter using biocompatible silicone-based glue.
Glue one end of the fiber sample to the back of the cover slip, wrap around the coverslip, then glue the free end to the back as well.
Place the fiber samples in a 24-well plate.
Sterilize the samples by immersing in 80% ethanol for 1 hr.
Rinse ethanol from samples using DI water.
Pipette 2 ml of basal medium onto samples to cover entirely.
Remove medium after 5 minutes.
Seed fibroblast 3T3 cells on fiber samples.
Suspend cells in DMEM with antibiotics and 10% FBS at a concentration of approximately 62,000 cells/cm² per 1 ml of DMEM.
Drop 1 ml of the cell-containing DMEM solution into each well plate to cover fiber samples with about 62,000 cells/cm².
Incubate well plates for 24 hours at 37 °C and 5% CO₂.
Cut dried PCL/keratin nanofiber membranes into squares approximately 30 mm x 30 mm.
Sterilize the samples with 80% alcohol for 10 minutes, then wash thoroughly with DI water.
Incubate samples in 15 ml of PBS at pH 7.5 and 37 °C.
Replace buffer every three days.
Remove membranes from solution after one week and seven weeks and rinse with DI water.
Place membrane samples into freeze dryer ampoules.
Seal the ampoules and create a vacuum by turning the knob.
Lyophilize for 24 hours until completely dry.
Attach dried samples to a SEM stage using copper tape.
Coat samples with gold at 15 mA for one minute and thirty seconds in the sputter coater.
Load the sample into the chamber of the SEM.
Observe the fiber samples at an accelerating voltage of 1.5 kV and 5 µA current.
